Analysis of Data¶

Ques. How many females visited the restaurant on each day?

In [215]:
female_grp = df.groupby('sex').get_group('Female')
In [216]:
female_grp.head()
Out[216]:
total_bill tip sex smoker day time size
0 16.99 1.01 Female No Sun Dinner 2
4 24.59 3.61 Female No Sun Dinner 4
11 35.26 5.00 Female No Sun Dinner 4
14 14.83 3.02 Female No Sun Dinner 2
16 10.33 1.67 Female No Sun Dinner 3
In [217]:
sns.countplot(x='day', data=female_grp, color='orange')
plt.title('Female Visit Count on Each Day')
plt.show()

Ques. How many males visited the restaurant for Dinner and Lunch?

In [218]:
male_grp = df.groupby('sex').get_group('Male')
sns.countplot(x='time' , data=male_grp, color='red')
plt.show()

Ques. What is the percentage of average total_bill paid by both smokers and non-smokers? Draw a pie chart.

In [227]:
smoker_grp = df.groupby('smoker')
sm_bill = smoker_grp.get_group('Yes')['total_bill'].mean()
non_sm_bill = smoker_grp.get_group('No')['total_bill'].mean()
In [228]:
sm_bill, non_sm_bill

(20.756344086021507, 19.18827814569536)

labels = ['Smokers', 'Non-Smokers']
values = [sm_bill, non_sm_bill]
In [230]:
plt.pie(values, labels=labels, autopct='%0.2f%%', colors=sns.color_palette('Set2'))
plt.title('Distribution of Average Bill')
plt.show()

Use of 'hue' parameter¶

It helps in visualizing the data based on different categories from a particular column by dividing it.

In [232]:
# without hue
sns.kdeplot(x='total_bill', data=df)
plt.show()
In [233]:
# with hue
sns.kdeplot(x='total_bill', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.show()
In [234]:
sns.boxplot(y='total_bill', data=df, hue='smoker')
plt.show()
In [235]:
sns.boxplot(y='total_bill', data=df, hue='day')
plt.show()
In [236]:
sns.countplot(x='day', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.show()
In [237]:
sns.scatterplot(x='total_bill', y='tip', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.show()

Subplots¶

We use subplot for visualizing multiple plots on a single chart

syntax- plt.subplot(row, column, cell)

In [238]:
plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))

plt.subplot(1,2,1)
sns.scatterplot(x='total_bill', y='tip', data=df, hue='sex')

plt.subplot(1,2,2)
sns.countplot(x='day', data=df, hue='sex')

plt.show()
In [239]:
plt.figure(figsize=(6,10))

plt.subplot(2,1,1)
sns.scatterplot(x='total_bill', y='tip', data=df, hue='sex')

plt.subplot(2,1,2)
sns.countplot(x='day', data=df, hue='sex')

plt.show()
In [240]:
plt.figure(figsize=(16,12))

plt.subplot(2,3,1)
sns.boxplot(y='total_bill', data=df, hue='day')
plt.title('Distribution of bill day wise')

plt.subplot(2,3,2)
plt.pie(values, labels=labels, autopct='%0.2f%%', colors=sns.color_palette('Set2'))
plt.title('Distribution of bill for smokers & non-smokers')

plt.subplot(2,3,3)
sns.scatterplot(x='total_bill', y='tip', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Relationship between total bill & tip')

plt.subplot(2,3,4)
sns.kdeplot(x='total_bill', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Dsitribution of bill gender-wise')

plt.subplot(2,3,5)
sns.barplot(x='day', y='tip', data=df, color='skyblue')
plt.title('Average tip given day-wise')

plt.subplot(2,3,6)
sns.countplot(x='day', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Count of customers visited each day gender-wise')

plt.show()
Adding a Title to the main chart¶
In [241]:
plt.figure(figsize=(16,12)).suptitle("Analysis of Customer Data for a Restaurant", fontsize=20)

plt.subplot(2,3,1)
sns.boxplot(y='total_bill', data=df, hue='day')
plt.title('Distribution of bill day wise')

plt.subplot(2,3,2)
plt.pie(values, labels=labels, autopct='%0.2f%%', colors=sns.color_palette('Set2'))
plt.title('Distribution of bill for smokers & non-smokers')

plt.subplot(2,3,3)
sns.scatterplot(x='total_bill', y='tip', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Relationship between total bill & tip')

plt.subplot(2,3,4)
sns.kdeplot(x='total_bill', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Dsitribution of bill gender-wise')
plt.xlabel('Bill Data')

plt.subplot(2,3,5)
sns.barplot(x='day', y='tip', data=df, color='skyblue')
plt.title('Average tip given day-wise')
plt.grid()

plt.subplot(2,3,6)
sns.countplot(x='day', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Count of customers visited each day gender-wise')

plt.show()

Saving the figure

In [242]:
plt.figure(figsize=(16,12)).suptitle("Analysis of Customer Data for a Restaurant", fontsize=20)

plt.subplot(2,3,1)
sns.boxplot(y='total_bill', data=df, hue='day')
plt.title('Distribution of bill day wise')

plt.subplot(2,3,2)
plt.pie(values, labels=labels, autopct='%0.2f%%', colors=sns.color_palette('Set2'))
plt.title('Distribution of bill for smokers & non-smokers')

plt.subplot(2,3,3)
sns.scatterplot(x='total_bill', y='tip', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Relationship between total bill & tip')

plt.subplot(2,3,4)
sns.kdeplot(x='total_bill', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Dsitribution of bill gender-wise')

plt.subplot(2,3,5)
sns.barplot(x='day', y='tip', data=df, color='skyblue')
plt.title('Average tip given day-wise')

plt.subplot(2,3,6)
sns.countplot(x='day', data=df, hue='sex')
plt.title('Count of customers visited each day gender-wise')

plt.savefig('Customer Data Dashboard.jpeg')
plt.show()
